items.headline: Semiconductors rout on Nov 5: Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down more than 12%, Nvidia down 9.3% (worst day since Jan 2025)
items.why: Memory and storage names fell hardest (SanDisk about -22%, Micron about -17%) even though both remain among 2026's top S&P 500 performers, so the AI hardware trade is being repriced on policy risk rather than on earnings; one bank called the move reactionary, and premarket on Nov 6 showed a partial rebound.

items.headline: Data-center build-out becomes a political variable: five states holding 37% of planned US capacity elected governors who campaigned on pausing or taxing it
items.why: US electricity prices are up about 10% since early 2024, so power cost and local permitting, not chip supply, are now the likeliest brake on AI capacity timelines.

items.headline: Bitcoin fell about 6% to roughly $75,600 and Ether about 7.8% to roughly $2,230 on Nov 6, after a one-day bounce; total market cap near $2.65 trillion
items.why: Crypto traded as a high-beta risk asset alongside the Nasdaq selloff, and the Fear & Greed index dropped from 50 to 28 in a day, which shows how fast sentiment is swinging with equities.

items.why: Hormuz shipping remains the main swing factor for crude and refined products; refined products stayed tight even as crude fell on deal hopes.

items.headline: Worst week for commodities since April 2025: Bloomberg Commodity Total Return Index down about 4.5%, energy down about 9%, Brent and WTI each down close to 13%
items.why: Crude fell on hopes of a US-Iran deal even though the index is still up about 27% year to date, and European gas fell about 16%, its biggest weekly drop in over a year.

items.headline: Gold rose about 5% on the week, silver about 5.7% and platinum about 6.8%, rebounding after gold broke below $3,970
items.why: Lower Treasury yields, a softer dollar and short covering drove the bounce; the source flags $3,970-3,975 as the pivot zone and a sustained move above $4,225 as the sign selling has run its course, and all four precious metals are still lower year to date.

items.headline: Copper fell more than 4% to its lowest since July, then rebounded
items.why: Traders priced in possible delays to AI data-center projects and lower odds of US tariffs on refined copper, while physical supply stays tight with weak Chilean output, so price and physical market are pulling in opposite directions.
